To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the strain in the vicinity of the weld seam during laser welding of aluminum alloys exhibits strain signatures which are related to the onset of centerline cracks.
the strain in the solidifying material is characterized by a strong compressive strain in the longitudinal direction, and a strong tensile strain in the transverse direction.
the strain signatures of hot cracks are characterized by a sudden strain drop followed by a strain recovery, and that the formation of hot crack is related to the occurrence of a strain drop.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: The influence of the laser beam power on the strain evolution The influence of the welding speed on the strain evolution
the development of a new method for the determination of the strain field in the immediate vicinity (1 mm) of the solidification boundary in laser beam welded aluminum sheets.
the following topics: • Development of an experimental setup to determine the local surface displacement near the weld seam of aluminum sheets during laser beam welding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
centerline cracks are formed in two steps: First, the strain rate is increased by an order of magnitude and then, the strain rate drops to a lower level.
hot cracking is a consequence of the formation of a solidification front that is unstable in a plane perpendicular to the welding direction.

the formation of center line cracks in laser beam welded aluminum alloy sheets is associated with a strain state that is dominated by a strong compressive component in the direction of the welding direction and by a high tensile strain in perpendicular direction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crack formation is associated with a local reduction of the strain.
a combination of a high temperature and a high strain rate in a certain range of the strain values is a prerequisite for the formation of hot cracking.
the strain signature of the formation of hot centerline cracks is a characteristic feature of the welding process that can be determined by the analysis of the strain distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hot cracking is associated to an abrupt increase in the strain, and that the strain is not necessarily a function of time.
the formation of center line hot cracks is related to a local strain relaxation in the immediate vicinity to the weld seam.
the onset of centerline cracks is preceded by the formation of strain signatures which are associated to the development of a tensile strain component in the weld centerline.
